description: Nature-inspired and soft-computing methods for search, optimisation and learning: evolutionary algorithms, genetic programming, swarm intelligence, fuzzy systems, artificial immune systems, neuro-evolution and multi-objective optimisation. Students implement each method, visualise its search behaviour and compare algorithms with sound statistics on benchmark and African application problems.
modelledOn: Eiben and Smith, Introduction to Evolutionary Computing
Poli, Langdon and McPhee, A Field Guide to Genetic Programming
Deb, Multi-Objective Optimization using Evolutionary Algorithms
outcomes: Implement genetic algorithms, evolution strategies and differential evolution and tune their operators and parameters.
Evolve programs and symbolic models with genetic programming while controlling bloat.
Apply particle swarm and ant colony optimisation to continuous and combinatorial problems.
Design, tune and evaluate fuzzy inference systems and immune-inspired detectors.
Evolve neural network weights and topologies, and solve multi-objective problems with Pareto-based methods.
Compare stochastic algorithms with proper experimental design and statistical tests and report reproducibly.

units.title: Search landscapes and baselines
topics: Fitness landscapes, local optima, ruggedness and the no free lunch theorems
Benchmark functions (sphere, Rastrigin, Rosenbrock) and performance measures
Hill climbing, random restarts and simulated annealing
Exploration versus exploitation and selection pressure

units.title: Evolutionary algorithms
topics: Genetic algorithms: representation, fitness-proportional and tournament selection, crossover and mutation
Evolution strategies, self-adaptation and CMA-ES
Evolutionary programming and differential evolution
Schema theorem, building blocks, premature convergence, diversity maintenance and niching
Constraint handling and parameter control

units.title: Genetic programming
topics: Tree representation, function and terminal sets, and initialisation
Subtree crossover and mutation; bloat and parsimony pressure
Symbolic regression and model discovery from data
Grammatical evolution and Cartesian genetic programming
Applications: evolved classifiers, controllers and rules

units.title: Swarm intelligence
topics: Particle swarm optimisation: velocity update, inertia weight, neighbourhood topologies and stability
Ant colony optimisation for the travelling salesman problem and routing: pheromone and heuristic information
Artificial bee colony, firefly and other swarm metaphors, and a critical view of them
Stigmergy, flocking and swarm robotics
Applications: delivery routing in Accra traffic and irrigation scheduling

units.title: Fuzzy systems
topics: Fuzzy sets, membership functions, set operations and alpha-cuts
Fuzzy rules, Mamdani inference and defuzzification methods
Rule-consequent (TSK-type) models and adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference
Fuzzy control design: irrigation, traffic signals and cold-room thermostats
Type-2 fuzzy sets and rough sets in outline

units.title: Artificial immune systems
topics: Immune inspiration: clonal selection, negative selection and immune networks
Clonal selection algorithms for optimisation
Negative selection for anomaly and fault detection
Danger theory and the dendritic cell algorithm

units.title: Neuro-evolution
topics: Evolving weights versus topologies; direct and indirect encodings
NEAT: innovation numbers, speciation and complexification
CPPNs and HyperNEAT for large regular networks
Evolution strategies as a scalable alternative to gradient reinforcement learning; neural architecture search
Novelty search, quality-diversity and MAP-Elites

units.title: Multi-objective optimisation
topics: Pareto dominance, Pareto fronts and trade-off analysis
NSGA-II: non-dominated sorting and crowding distance
Decomposition and indicator-based methods: MOEA/D, SPEA2 and the hypervolume
Many-objective problems and decision making; crop planning case
Memetic algorithms and hybridisation with local search

units.title: Experimental method and project
topics: Experimental design for stochastic algorithms: runs, seeds, budgets and statistical tests (Wilcoxon, Friedman)
Reproducible reporting, ablation and parameter sensitivity
Choosing a method for a problem; hyper-heuristics and algorithm selection
Project presentation and critique

schedule.title: Search landscapes and baselines
schedule.exercise: Plot the landscape of Rastrigin in two dimensions, explain why hill climbing stalls, and compare restarts with annealing at equal evaluation budgets.

tasks.title: Plot Sphere, Rastrigin and Rosenbrock in two dimensions and mark their global optima and the number of visible local optima
Implement hill climbing with random restarts and simulated annealing on Rastrigin in 10 dimensions and compare best fitness over 30 runs
Sweep the annealing cooling rate on a travelling salesman instance and plot final tour length against rate to show the exploration and exploitation balance

schedule.title: Genetic algorithms and evolution strategies
schedule.exercise: Hand-simulate one generation of a genetic algorithm on a 6-bit one-max problem, and explain how self-adaptation changes a mutation step size.

tasks.title: Step through three generations of a genetic algorithm on a bit-string problem and record selection, crossover points and mutations for each offspring
Implement a genetic algorithm for 0/1 knapsack with tournament selection and compare one-point and uniform crossover over 30 runs
Implement a (mu, lambda) evolution strategy with self-adaptive step sizes on Rosenbrock and plot step size and fitness against generation

schedule.title: Differential evolution, diversity and constraints
schedule.exercise: Explain the DE/rand/1 mutation, why diversity collapse causes premature convergence, and two ways to handle constraints.

tasks.title: Implement differential evolution with rand/1/bin and run it on Rastrigin in 20 dimensions, recording the best fitness every 50 generations
Run a genetic algorithm on a deceptive function with and without fitness sharing, and plot population diversity to see niches form
Solve a constrained design problem with penalty functions and with a repair operator and compare feasibility rate and final quality over 30 runs

schedule.title: Genetic programming
schedule.exercise: Draw two parent trees, show a subtree crossover, and suggest three ways to control bloat in a symbolic regression run.

tasks.title: Build random expression trees from a function and terminal set, evaluate them on five inputs, and apply subtree crossover to two parents
Run symbolic regression to recover a hidden formula from noisy data, using parsimony pressure, and compare accuracy and tree size with and without it
Evolve a rule set for classifying crop disease records with grammatical evolution and compare its test accuracy with a decision tree

schedule.title: Particle swarm and ant colony optimisation
schedule.exercise: Compute one particle update by hand with inertia, cognitive and social terms, and explain how pheromone evaporation avoids stagnation.

tasks.title: Watch a 20-particle swarm on a 2D function, change the inertia weight and topology, and note convergence speed and premature collapse
Step ant colony optimisation on a 12-city tour, show the pheromone matrix after each iteration, and compare the best tour with the optimum
Tune inertia and acceleration coefficients of particle swarm on Rastrigin by a grid search and identify the stable region of parameters

schedule.title: Swarm variants and applications
schedule.exercise: Critique a new metaphor-based swarm algorithm for novelty, and plan a vehicle routing model for deliveries in Accra.

tasks.title: Simulate boids with separation, alignment and cohesion rules and describe how changing the weights changes flock patterns
Use ant colony optimisation to route 15 deliveries in a city with different travel times, and compare the route with nearest-neighbour
Compare an artificial bee colony and a basic particle swarm on five benchmarks over 30 runs and test whether any difference is significant

schedule.title: Fuzzy sets and inference
schedule.exercise: Define membership functions for temperature and humidity, evaluate three Mamdani rules for one input, and defuzzify by centroid.

tasks.title: Plot triangular and Gaussian membership functions for soil moisture, then compute union, intersection and complement of two fuzzy sets
Step a Mamdani inference for one input through fuzzification, rule firing, aggregation and centroid defuzzification, and read the crisp output
Compare centroid, bisector and mean-of-maxima defuzzification on a rule base for fan speed and plot the three control surfaces

schedule.title: Fuzzy modelling and control
schedule.exercise: Design a fuzzy controller for drip irrigation and compare its behaviour with a simple on-off controller.

tasks.title: Fit a TSK-type fuzzy model to crop yield data and compare its error with a linear regression on a held-out test set
Build a fuzzy controller for a cold-room thermostat, simulate a hot afternoon, and compare temperature stability and energy use with on-off control
Tune membership function widths of a fuzzy traffic-light controller with a genetic algorithm to reduce average queue length in a simulated junction

schedule.title: Artificial immune systems
schedule.exercise: Contrast clonal selection with negative selection, and explain how a detector set trained on normal behaviour can flag a fault.

tasks.title: Step a clonal selection algorithm on a multimodal function and record the clones, hypermutation and affinity of the best antibodies per generation
Generate detectors by negative selection from normal sensor readings and measure detection and false alarm rates on injected faults
Implement the dendritic cell algorithm on a labelled network log and compare its detection against negative selection on the same data

schedule.title: Evolving neural networks
schedule.exercise: Compare direct and indirect encodings, and explain how NEAT uses innovation numbers to line up genes during crossover.

tasks.title: Evolve the weights of a fixed small neural net to solve XOR with a genetic algorithm and watch the fitness and weights change
Step through NEAT on the XOR problem, showing mutations that add nodes and links, species, and the champion network per generation
Use a CPPN to generate the weight pattern of a layer from node coordinates and compare its size and accuracy with a directly encoded net

schedule.title: Scalable neuro-evolution and quality-diversity
schedule.exercise: Compare gradient-based reinforcement learning with evolution strategies on a control task, and discuss why novelty search can beat objective-based search.

tasks.title: Train a small policy on a balance task with evolution strategies using 50 perturbations per update and plot return against environment steps
Run novelty search on a deceptive maze and compare it with fitness-based search on the number of goals reached over 20 runs
Implement MAP-Elites for a simulated robot gait with two behaviour descriptors and plot the elite map after 5,000 evaluations

schedule.title: Multi-objective optimisation
schedule.exercise: Sort a set of ten solutions into Pareto fronts, compute crowding distance, and discuss how to pick one solution from a front for a farmer.

tasks.title: Compute Pareto dominance for 20 candidate solutions of two objectives, plot the front, and mark the dominated points
Step NSGA-II through two generations, showing non-dominated sorting, crowding distance and the selected survivors
Optimise a crop planning problem for profit, water use and labour with NSGA-II and compare the hypervolume with a weighted-sum approach

schedule.title: Experimental method and project
schedule.exercise: Plan and report a fair comparison of two algorithms with equal budgets, 30 seeds and a Wilcoxon test, and present your project.

tasks.title: Run two optimisers on 5 benchmarks with 30 seeds each and report medians, interquartile ranges and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test per function
Plot convergence curves with confidence bands and a parameter sensitivity heatmap for your chosen algorithm, and state what the data supports
Implement a simple algorithm selector that chooses between GA and DE from problem features and evaluate it against always choosing one method
